title: Born on September 7th, the woman who built a bank for India's poorest workers.
sources: Britannica - Ela Bhatt biography, birth date September 7, 1933
MapsOfIndia - 7th September 1933: Ela Bhatt, Founder of Self-Employed Women's Association of India, is Born
caption:
Born on September 7th, the woman who built a bank for India's poorest workers.

Born in Ahmedabad in 1933, Bhatt trained as a lawyer and joined India's oldest textile workers' union in 1955. In 1972, inspired by Gandhi, she founded the Self-Employed Women's Association - SEWA - to organize India's informal-sector women workers.

In 1974, SEWA set up a cooperative bank to give small loans to poor women starting their own businesses - vendors, artisans, laborers with no collateral and no credit history. By the mid-1990s, SEWA had grown into India's largest single union, with nearly 220,000 members.

Millions of India's workers still operate outside formal systems - without credit, insurance or a union behind them. Bhatt's model proved that including them isn't charity, it's how a much larger share of the economy gets counted, financed and grown.
